messages.subject: readCdfGroupNames
parts:
Hi,
I guess this is actually from the affxparser package, but I don't
understand why I'm getting "" as group names for the following:

> readCdfGroupNames(getPathname(cdf),units=units)
$`4056650`
[1] ""
> stratifyIndices <- readCdfCellIndices(getPathname(cdf), units =
units, stratifyBy = stratifyBy)
> stratifyIndices
$`4056650`
$`4056650`$groups
$`4056650`$groups$`4056650`
$`4056650`$groups$`4056650`$indices
[1] 4145867 2309057 4606959 5528889 3993011 1644175 766455 2613403
5783619 5604411 1201361

Isn't the group name the same as the unit name -- i.e. no groups?
('4056650'). Or does the function just not return the group name if it
is the same as the unit name?

Thanks,
Elizabeth

messages.author: 0e065001d5e74ca3
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] readCdfGroupNames
parts:
Hi,

Henrik posted about this a couple of days ago (see post titled "Finding
units from cells"). Basically affxparser strips unit names from group
names. Because the group names ARE the unit names for single-group units
for the exon array, you get an empty string. That's why you have to use
the workaround I showed you. This is fixed in the latest affxparser (not
sure if it is up yet), where you can set argument truncateGroupNames=FALSE
to avoid this.

Cheers,

Ken

That argument is going to be available in affxparser v1.7.5, which I
committed to BioC earlier today, that is, expect it to be available
within the next 24 hours.

There reason for stripping of prefix of the group names that matches
the unit name is/was 1) to make names from binary and ASCII CDF files
be the same, because for SNP chips the unit names were part of the
group names in ASCII version, but not the binary version, and 2) to
save RAM because repeating unit names uses a large fraction of what is
returned.

messages.author: a5f6afcbe5b17914
messages.subject: Re: readCdfGroupNames
parts:
FYI,

affxparser v1.7.5 is now available on BioC devel. Update this package
as you did to install it, see aroma.affymetrix group page for details.

FOR DEVELOPERS:
The only new thing is that the before default removal of unit names
from the group names in readCdfGroupNames() is now optional via
argument 'truncateGroupNames'. Examples below.

Implementation guidelines: Please please minimize direct calls to
affxparser in aroma.affymetrix. It is better to provide on method in
a aroma.affymetrix class, which you then call. The reason for this is
to minimize the interface to other packages which makes it is easier
to maintain. Be also aware that classes that merge groups etc has to
be implemented specially, and cannot rely on a simple call to
affxparser. See also last Example 2 for a last warning.

EXAMPLE 1: (Example as expected)

> cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("Mapping250K_Nsp");
> pathname <- getPathname(cdf)
> readCdfGroupNames(pathname, units=1)
$`AFFX-5Q-123`
[1] ""

> readCdfGroupNames(pathname, units=1, truncateGroupNames=FALSE)
$`AFFX-5Q-123`
[1] "AFFX-5Q-123"


EXAMPLE 2: (Differences between ASCII and binary CDFs for SNP chips)

Note, although it is the same chip type, binary and ASCII CDFs contain
different group names as illustrated below. (This is why I/we decided
to truncate the unit names in all cases to always get the same
result).

# Reading a binary CDF
> readCdfGroupNames(pathname, units=100)
$`SNP_A-1782949`
[1] "A" "G"
> readCdfGroupNames(pathname, units=100, truncateGroupNames=FALSE)
$`SNP_A-1782949`
[1] "A" "G"

# Reading an ASCII CDF
> readCdfGroupNames(pathname, units=100)
$`SNP_A-1782949`
[1] "SNP_A-1782949A" "SNP_A-1782949G"
> readCdfGroupNames(pathname, units=100, truncateGroupNames=FALSE)
$`SNP_A-1782949`
[1] "A" "G"

Cheers

Henrik
